page: The Vultr vcg-l40s-16c-180g-48vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with an Intel Xeon 6448H processor. This x86_64 CPU features 16 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model and no hyperthreading. The system is equipped with 180.0 GB of system memory, providing 11.25 GB per core. Graphics processing and parallel computing workloads are accelerated by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, which includes 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 1200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data highlights the server's capabilities in parallel processing and machine learning tasks. The NVIDIA L40S GPU delivers top-tier performance in large language model inference, achieving 13631.52 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model and 6293.73 tokens per second on a medium 7B model. Text generation speeds reach 610.8 tokens per second and 153.1 tokens per second for the 135M and 7B models, respectively. CPU-bound tasks show strong performance, with bzip3 single-threaded decompression reaching 15.59 GB/sec and multi-threaded decompression at 238.14 GB/sec. Standard system operations, such as Redis SET operations at 41.33 million operations per second and Passmark database operations, fall within the average performance tier.

Given its hardware profile, this server offers a resource-dense configuration suitable for memory-intensive and GPU-accelerated workloads. The combination of 180.0 GB of RAM and 48 GB of VRAM makes it highly efficient for medium-scale LLM inference, data science pipelines, and parallel decompression tasks. However, the shared CPU allocation model and 2.0 GHz clock speed represent a tradeoff for workloads requiring dedicated, high-frequency single-core CPU performance. The server is best suited for machine learning inference, data processing, and database workloads that leverage GPU acceleration and high memory capacity.
